chapter: Vaudeville and the name Mac and Mac
title: Vaudeville in New York: staying on past the first half
summary: Mary tells how in New York in 1914 they were afraid of being hooked, but kept their act and were held over for weeks at the Lincoln and the Howard. Billy recalls String Beans, Butler May and the Whitman sisters, and how the Northern acts first looked down on them.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Go ahead and answer that. I can turn this off for a minute. Unless you want to keep, one of you keep talking. It's all right.

When you go to New York, you know, you'd get a half of...the first half. Yes. Of the whole...the whole...the first half. And then somebody else had the second half. Well, then instead of us getting just the first half, we'd have the first half. And they'd say, can you change your act for the second half? Yes. Then can you change for next week? And would you see that in New York at the Lincoln Theater and Washington at the Howard Theater and all of those theaters. Well, instead of keeping us just the three days or four days, well, they'd keep us two and three weeks. Stay on. Uh-huh. And a southern act, too, you know.
What do you want? If you want to answer the phone, it's all right. I can turn this off for a while.
No, that's all right. It's gone now.
Oh. I was telling him about the vaudeville and String Beans.
Oh, yeah. Butler May. I read about him.

Yes. He said, Mac, come to New York. You come to New York. And that was 1914 when we went to New York. Yeah. And we were so scared, you know, that we were going to get fired, or canned, get the hook. You know, they had a hook that they would grab you. Oh, yeah, it is. Yeah. And the Whitman sisters, they were there with us. They were not there with us, but they were in New York.

And they would come with the suitcases. So when they'd canned an act, all they had to do was come out the audience and come on, you see, ready. So we just thought that we were going to get, I did, not Mac. Mac was always, he said, just do the act like we've always did it. And I said, well, they don't have acts like that. He said, do the act like we've always done our act. And we did. And when the man come to the dressing room door and knocked, you know, I thought he was putting the pictures under the door. And he asked about the, for the next half.
Well, we had a repertoire of changes, you know.
